title: Retail Installment Contracts Training Q&A: The Remaining-Term Allowance on Hardship Deferrals
content:
*What is the remaining-term allowance on a Retail Installment Contracts hardship extension agreement?*

It is an allowance set by the installments remaining on the contract. The installments remaining are the monthly due dates from the next due date through the final installment date (maturity date), both included.

- With at least **13** installments remaining, the allowance is the tier's maximum installments deferred by one extension.
- With no more than **3** remaining, the allowance is zero.
- In between — 4 through 12 remaining — it is **one** installment.

*How are the installments remaining counted?*

Count the next due date itself and every monthly due date after it up to and including the final installment date.

| Next due date | Final installment date | Installments remaining | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 March | 15 May of the same year | 3 | zero |
| 15 March | 15 June of the same year | 4 | one installment |
| 15 March | 15 February of the next year | 12 | one installment |
| 15 March | 15 March of the next year | 13 | the tier's per-request maximum |

*Does an earlier extension change the count?* Only through the dates: an extension moves the next due date and the final installment date, and the count is taken from the dates the contract carries on the signing date.
